# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 9 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus (ch 1-31) / P.Mich. 130 (ch 32+), Shepherd of Hermas 9 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_009_page_001.jpg

---

## Vision 3, Chapter 1

**1** The third vision which I saw, brothers and sisters, was as follows. **2** After I had fasted many times and prayed to the Lord to show me the revelation he had promised through the aged woman — that very night she appeared to me and said, "Because you are so persistent and eager to know all things, come out to the field where you farm around the fifth hour, and I will appear to you and show you what you need to see." **3** I asked, "Lady, which part of the field?" She replied, "Wherever you wish — only choose a quiet place." And before I could say where, she said, "I will come wherever you are." **4** I went to the field, brothers and sisters, counted the hours, and came to the place I had chosen. I saw an ivory couch there with a linen pillow on it and a fine linen covering over it. **5** When I found these things lying there with no one in the place, I was struck with wonder; a trembling came upon me and my hair stood on end. When I recovered, I saw the aged woman approaching with a book in her hand. She sat down alone and greeted me: "Greetings, man of God." I was filled with grief and broke into weeping. **6** She asked me, "Why are you weeping?" I said, "Because, my lady, I do not know if I will be able to endure to the end." She answered, "Be confident — you have been appointed by the Lord to endure the trials of this world, for your own sake and for the sake of your household. Take courage." **7** I said, "Lady, show me the vision." She replied, "Do you want to see it right now?" "My lady, I am greatly longing for it," I said. She reached out and touched me, and I felt as if I had just come from a bath. **8** "Come then," she said. And I saw before me the things I had seen before — the great tower being built with brilliant squared stones.

---

### Council Notes

The address "man of God" (v. 5) marks a significant elevation in Hermas's status. In the Hebrew Bible this title belongs to prophets — Moses (Deut 33:1), Elijah (1 Kgs 17:18), Elisha (2 Kgs 4:7). In the NT it appears in 1 Timothy 6:11 and 2 Timothy 3:17. Hermas is being positioned in the prophetic succession.

The touching and sense of purification (v. 7) resonates with prophetic call narratives (Isaiah 6; Ezekiel 1-2) where the prophet is prepared/purified before receiving the vision.

The triple visionary structure (Visions 1, 2, 3) with the same ivory couch setting creates a liturgical pattern — as if Hermas is regularly summoned to the same "heavenly office" to receive instruction.
